  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. (MAKEUP) EXAMINATIONS - JUNE/JULY 2023  
  SUBJECT: ECE 1071-PHY/ECE_1071-B/ECE 1051-B - BASIC ELECTRONICS  
  
  BASIC ELECTRONICS [ECE 1071-PHY]  
  Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  Answer ALL questions.  
  Missing data may be suitably assumed.  
  1A)          A silicon diode is forward biased by 0.65V, and has a reverse saturation current of 12nA  
  at 200C. Calculate,  
  i) Diode current.                                                                        (4)  
  ii) Static and Dynamic resistance.  
  iii) Diode current when the temperature rises to 1000C.  
  
  1B)          Draw V-I characteristics of the 'Si' diode. Explain the different types of breakdowns that  
  can occur in a PN junction diode.                                                          (3)  
  
  1C)          Calculate the bias current of MOSFET shown in the figure below. Assume μnCox = 80  
  μA/V2 and VTH = 0.4 V. If the gate voltage increases by 20 mV, what is the change in  
  the drain voltage?  
  
  
  (3)  
  
  
  2A)          Explain the operation of a center-tapped Full Wave Rectifier with a neat circuit diagram  
  and waveforms. Derive the equation for Vdc, Vrms and efficiency considering ideal        (4)  
  diodes.  
  
  2B)          A half-wave rectifier with a capacitor filter is supplied from a transformer having a peak  
  secondary voltage of 20V and frequency 50Hz. The load resistance is 560Ω and the  
  capacitor used is 1000μF. Calculate ripple factor and dc output voltage. Draw the filtered (3)  
  output and label peak and dc value.

  2C)             Draw the circuit of a Zener voltage regulator. The Zener diode in a regulator circuit has  
  a breakdown voltage of 15V, a minimum current of 1mA, and a power rating of 0.5W.  
  The series resistance connected in the circuit is 1kΩ. If the input voltage applied is 40V, (3)  
  find the range of load resistance that can be connected to prevent the Zener diode from  
  being destroyed.  
  
  3A)             i) With the help of a truth table, obtain the Boolean expression for a 4: 1 Multiplexer and  
  implement it using basic gates.                                                             (4)  
  ii) Perform (19.25)10 -(10.75)10 using 2's complement method.  
  
  3B)             Define CMRR for an OPAMP. When the voltage applied to the non-inverting terminal,  
  V1 is 0.25 mV and the voltage applied to the inverting terminal, V2 is - 0.25 mV, the  
  output voltage of the OPAMP is 4V. For the same OPAMP, when V1 = V2 = 0.5 mV, the (3)  
  output voltage is 6 mV. Calculate CMRR.  
  
  3C)             With a neat circuit diagram and relevant waveforms, explain the working of a square  
  wave generator.                                                                                (3)  
  
  4A)             A (7,4) bit Hamming code received is 0011101(P1P2D3P4D5D6D7), considering even  
  parity. Check for errors in the received code and if there is an error, write the corrected    (4)  
  code.  
  
  4B)             With a neat circuit diagram and truth table, explain the working of 4:1 multiplexer using  
  basic gates.                                                                              (3)  
  
  4C)             Design a 2-bit Ripple down counter using negative edge triggered JK Flipflop. Draw the  
  timing for the same.                                                                   (3)  
  
  5A)             An audio signal 20sin (2 100t) amplitude modulates a carrier of 40sin (2 200 × 103).  
  Find (a) modulation index (b) Sideband frequencies (c) Bandwidth (d) Amplitude of              (4)  
  each side band components.  
  
  5B)             For the given binary data 1101 sketch the ASK, FSK and PSK waveforms.  
  (3)  
  
  5C)             State the sampling theorem. For an analog signal, x(t) = 10cos200 t+2sin300 t-cos100  
  t. Determine the minimum sampling rate required to reconstruct the signal.         (3)
